scenes.headline: How to read a machine-checked theorem
scenes.sub: What Lean guarantees in OpenAI's math release
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lemma! OpenAI released hundreds of new theorems from one model. Here is how the checking works, and where it stops.

scenes.text: Comparator proves the proof matches the statement. Only a person can check that the statement matches the paper.
scenes.say: The machine checks that a proof proves the statement. A person must check that the statement says what the paper claims.

scenes.title: From a posed problem to a green tick

steps.say: The model was posed about four thousand problems, with about three hours of thinking for each result it kept.
For many results, agents also wrote a Lean proof. Nobody trusts that proof yet.
The claim lives in a separate statement file that imports only mathlib, and ends in sorry.
Comparator checks the proof states exactly that theorem, with only standard axioms, then replays it through the kernel.

scenes.title: Five layers of a green tick
scenes.say: A green tick has five layers. The machine owns three of them.

items.say: No extra axioms, and no sorry anywhere in the library.
The proof is about the exact statement in the file.
A person must read the statement against the paper.
And check it is the headline result, not a weaker corollary.

scenes.title: Which families come with Lean
scenes.say: Two hundred thirty five of the three hundred seventy two families have Lean. The rest are ordinary preprints, waiting for referees.

scenes.title: The proof that outgrew its target

steps.say: In the pi summary, the model aimed for five halves and reached a bound near two and a half.
Then its own inequality allowed any exponent above two, and it spent the next sections auditing that.

scenes.text: Short statements in plain mathlib are nearly settled once Comparator runs. Long statements and manuscript-only claims need specialists.
scenes.say: Short statements in plain mathlib are close to settled once Comparator runs. Long statements, and claims with no Lean, need specialists.
The machine checks the proof. People check the statement. And more than a third of the families have no Lean at all.
